title: PHP2Shell: How Security Teams Should Assess and Contain the Reported PHP RCEs
content_md: The hardest part of a critical infrastructure vulnerability is often finding every place where it is exposed. A company may know which applications use PHP, but not which PHP binaries actually serve those applications, which configuration files they load, or whether a public endpoint accepts request bodies the application never intended to process. That gap matters with the newly reported PHP2Shell issues, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . PHP has announced two critical security issues, each scored 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 . External research describes an unauthenticated remote-code-execution path in PHP’s multipart upload processing. The PHP project’s detailed advisory and exact affected-version matrix were not yet available when this article was prepared, before its scheduled October 21, 2026, 14:00 UTC security release. For defenders, the first task is therefore practical: establish where PHP executes, identify configurations that may reach the reported code path, and prepare to replace vulnerable runtimes as soon as vendor fixes are confirmed.
